NEXUS OS 4.1 -- QUICK HELP

YOUR SHIFT: your tasks are in the Work Queue (top right, or the Task button on the taskbar). Do them in order; the hint under each task says how. A task marked (remote session) was added by another session, not by Night Operations: you decide whether to do it. If you are stuck on a task (reading does not count), the hint comes again with the next step, and then Night Operations offers to finish it for you: Finish it or Not now. Work done by anyone else is marked with their name in the Work Queue and Work Orders.

OPEN: Double-click an icon or file to open it.
MOVE A WINDOW: Drag it by its title bar. Drag it to the left or right edge of the screen to fill that half (two programs side by side); drag it away to get its size back.
MOVE FILES: Double-click Workstation to open File Manager, click a folder on the left, then drag a file onto another folder. The status bar confirms each move, and the Work Queue lists each file of a task and where it is.
SHRED: Drag a file onto the Disposal bin, then click Yes.
WORK ORDERS: Look the owner up in Personnel, then click Approve or Reject.
TUG-OF-WAR: if session 017 (the dark arrow; yours is the white one) grabs a file you are dragging, keep the button held and pull the file into the Disposal bin. A rope runs from your pointer through the file to the other pointer. Every yank toward the bin reels the file closer; it drags the file back when you stop, and now and then it yanks hard (its pointer twitches first). Short, fast yanks win: move toward the bin, come back with the button still held, and yank again. Every fight starts with a short GET READY while it takes the other end. Once the file is more than half way, letting go keeps it. Let go before that and press the button again at once, or the other pointer keeps it. Options has Tug assist (Hold: holding the button is enough) and Click lock (click once to pick up, again to drop). Mail may tell you to let the other pointer finish: let it move things on its own, but when a task tells you to shred a file, fight for it.
JOTTER: if a remote session types to you in Jotter, type a reply and press Enter when the line under the text says Your turn. While it is typing, your reply waits and is sent when it stops. Your typing goes to the Jotter that is waiting for you, even when another window is in front.
CAMERAS: Camera Viewer shows the security cameras. Click a camera on the left to switch. Another session can close the viewer: double-click Camera Viewer to open it again, on the camera you picked last.
LOCKED FOLDERS: some folders ask for a code. Type the code and press Enter.
SAVING: some files can be changed in Jotter. Typing starts a new line at the end; use File > Save (or Ctrl+S) to keep it.
DAMAGED FILES: a .dat file opens in the Data Viewer as bytes. A damaged file also has a Recovered text button: it shows the readable words in the window's full width, and Hex view goes back.
NEXUS MENU: the Nexus button (bottom left) lists every program, Help and Shut Down. At the end of a shift it also holds Log Off.
OPTIONS: Right-click an item to see what you can do with it. Esc or the || button on the taskbar pauses the shift.
NOTICES: the last twenty are kept: Nexus menu, Recent notices. Options has an Accessibility page: notice time, relaxed timing (the timed moments last twice as long), sound captions, mono audio, a large cursor and a slower double-click.

NEXUS OS records all activity for quality purposes.

SECOND CURSOR

A game about sharing a desk with someone who never logged off.

Design, writing, code, pixel art and sound were made for this game. Every sound is generated while you play.

Made with Unity.

Letheworth Data Reclamation, NEXUS OS, Orrery Computing and everyone who works there are invented. Any resemblance to a real night shift is a coincidence.

Thanks to every night operator who tested an early build.

LOCKED FOLDERS: some folders ask for a code. Type the code and press Enter.
SAVING: some files can be changed in Jotter. Typing starts a new line at the end; use File > Save to keep it.
DAMAGED FILES: a .dat file opens in the Data Viewer as bytes. A damaged file also has a Recovered text button: it shows the readable words in the window's full width, and Hex view goes back.
NEXUS MENU: the Nexus button (bottom left) lists every program, Help and Shut Down. At the end of a shift it also holds Log Off.
TYPING: the on-screen keyboard opens by itself when you can type.
OPTIONS: Press L2 on an item to see what you can do with it. B or the Menu button pauses the shift.
